title: Managed identity — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, a reviewer asks where the application credential is stored. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences on where the credential lives, who can read it, and what rotation would cost today.

vocabulary.meaning: an identity granted by the platform to a running workload, so that no secret has to be stored or rotated
the work required to replace a secret everywhere it is used, which measures how expensive storing it really was

expectedElements: The storage location of the credential is explicit
The reader of the credential is identified
Rotation cost is stated rather than assumed to be zero
modelAnswer: The application does not store a database credential; it uses an identity issued by the platform at runtime. This means there is no secret in configuration or source control, and the evidence is that a search of the configuration returns no secret to rotate. The limitation is local development, where a developer still authenticates with a personal login that does have a rotation cost. I will document the local path separately so the difference is not assumed away.
commonMistakes: Answering that the credential is safe without saying where it is
Claiming a credentialless setup while local development still relies on a stored login
variants: Rewrite the update for an auditor who wants the list of identities with database access.
